title: Rule when instance is required on a component expectation
description:
KDATAP-08a0ac requires "canonical instance/vendor when known" plus "one strict all-required-fields result". The migration reading of "when known" decides whether the component number is usable or structurally zero.

All 563 component annotations carry a `subject.name`. For the 473 assets it is a code-level instance (`directus_users`, `LocalAuthDriver`, `UsersService`). If the migration reads those as the canonical instance field, 473 expectations acquire an instance requirement and the strict result stays near zero for exactly the 85% of gold that is otherwise satisfiable — the failure the decision exists to prevent, reintroduced by a plausible migration step.

Measured shape of component gold:

| gold key shape | instances | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `type:<taxonomy subtype id>` | 481 | 85% |
| `third_party:<vendor>` | 52 | 9% |
| `actor:user` (no declared subtype) | 30 | 5% |

**Proposed decision.** Instance is a required field only where gold asserts a vendor — the 52 `third_party:` cases. For assets and actors the strict result is (type, subtype), which is the whole claim those annotations make. Instance/vendor resolution is graded as its own diagnostic over the population that actually claims one.

**Corollary to state in the contract:** strict means all fields *gold asserts*, not all fields the schema defines. Otherwise "when known" gets implemented as "always required".

Rejected: treating asset `subject.name` as the canonical instance; requiring every schema field on every expectation.
